newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch toughen swine fever controls.
newsitem.headline: Dutch toughen swine fever controls.

text.p: The Dutch Farm Ministry said on Thursday it planned extra measures to control a swine fever epidemic in the south of the Netherlands that has so far lead to the slaughter of some 650,000 pigs.

Dutch Farm Minister Jozias van Aartsen announced the measures in a letter to parliament but action stops short of the massive pig cull involving one million animals that Dutch media predicted on Wednesday.
The new controls apply to around 1,600 farms nationwide that have received pig sperm from the infected area. These farms have now come under 'infected status', a ministry spokeswoman said.
"This means the controls are very strict and that at the slightest sign of swine fever at any of these farms, all pigs there will be destroyed," she said.

She also said that from now any new case of swine fever -- 89 have so far been discovered -- would lead the ministry to examine any farms with a connection to the affected one for the slightest possibility of infection.
"We think these new controls will prevent the disease from spreading," she said.
She confirmed that a request had been put to the Defence Ministry to help with any further culling that was deemed necessary but stressed that that was not yet needed.

Belgium on Thursday announced extra measures to prevent swine fever from spreading to its farms. Agriculture Minister Karel Pinxten imposed an immediate slaughter and ban on all husbandry animals in some towns near the Dutch border.
The latest outbreak of swine fever, first detected in February, is the Netherland's first since 1992. It is a highly contagious disease, although not harmful to humans.
Since the outbreak many of the country's trading partners including the United States have banned imports of Dutch pigs and pork products.
